rules_a_to_k.how: tm_site option 'The anterior mediastinum, the mediastinum with no part named, or the chest, and the report calls the tumour a thymoma, a thymic carcinoma or a thymic carcinoid' records Thymus (C37.9): the chest (C76.1) is an ill-defined region and the tumour type names the tissue. Its reason states the site.

tm_site option 'Beside the thymus or the mediastinum (for example perithymic), and the report does not call the tumour a thymic tumour type' records Thorax, NOS (C76.1). A thymic tumour type beside the thymus takes the thymus through the option above it, because the tumour type shows the tissue.
tm_site option 'More than one part of the mediastinum, and the report does not say where the tumour began' records Overlapping lesion of heart, mediastinum and pleura (C38.8), named in its reason.
Referral only: the lymphoma options on tm_histology and tm_cytology send the case to Group II, whose questions set the lymphoma's site.
tm_histology option 'T-lymphoblastic leukaemia' refers to Group I; its reason states that leukaemias are recorded at the bone marrow (C42.1).

tm_histology hint ('Record the behaviour the pathologist states') and the exclusion options: micronodular thymoma with lymphoid stroma (8580/1), and 'Microscopic thymoma, or a thymoma the report calls benign' (8580/0), whose reason says a thymoma called benign takes the benign code.

tm_picker hint ('When the report gives two grades of carcinoid or neuroendocrine tumour, pick the higher grade'): typical and atypical carcinoid in one tumour records 8249/3. The sixth digit is not built (registrar, 7 October 2026).

ICD-O-3.2 prints (C37.9) beside 8580-8586. tm_site hint and its second option record the thymus for a thymic tumour type when the report places it in the anterior mediastinum or mediastinum with no part named; the posterior mediastinum option and the 'Outside the mediastinum' option keep the site the report gives for an ectopic thymic tumour, including Intrapulmonary thymoma, which ICD-O-3.2 prints with (C34._). The deposit option on tm_histology covers the check that the stated site is not a metastasis.
Every WHO thymus and mediastinum name maps to an ICD-O-3.2 term or to a code the WHO table prints; no name needs its word roots reordered.

tm_histology hint: more than one thymoma type in one tumour takes the higher code (A 8581 < AB 8582 < B1 8583 < B2 8584 < B3 8585). tm_picker hint: two tumour types with no entry covering both take the higher code. conflicts.issue: The WHO thymus table lists carcinosarcoma 8980/3 as a subtype of sarcomatoid carcinoma, but ICCC-2017 places 8980 in XIIa4 at every site. The thymus tree refers it to Group XII.
Registration without tissue (basis 1 or 2) and cytology that names no type record 8000/3, which ICCC-2017 places in XIIb at C37.9 and C38. These cases count in Group XII, not Group XI.
A carcinoma arising in a mediastinal teratoma is Teratoma with somatic-type malignancies 9084/3, Group X (Xb2), not a Group XI carcinoma. Every mediastinal germ cell tumour refers to Group X.
ICD-O-3.2 codes immature teratoma of thymus 9080/1, and the WHO mediastinal table agrees; ICCC-2017 Xb2 at C37.9 takes /3 only. Group X decides whether it is registered.

NUT carcinomas can express SALL4 and alpha-fetoprotein and be mistaken for germ cell tumours, and germ cell tumours can express wild-type NUT protein and be mistaken for NUT carcinoma (Marx 2022, PDF p. 10). The tool records the final diagnosis the report states.

Mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma and T-lymphoblastic lymphoma present as thymic or mediastinal masses, and the lymphoid component of type B thymoma can raise the suspicion of T-lymphoblastic lymphoma. ICCC-2017 places 9679/3 in IIb2 and 9837/3 in IIb1 at these sites.

T-lymphoblastic leukaemia is coded to the bone marrow (Rule E) and ICCC-2017 places 9837/3 there in Ia1; the same code at C37.9 or C38 is IIb1. The histology screen offers the leukaemia and the lymphoma as separate referrals.
Neuroblastoma, ganglioneuroblastoma and extra-adrenal paraganglioma occur in the posterior mediastinum. ICCC-2017 places 9500 and 9490 in IVa and 8693/3 in IVb.
Mediastinal sarcomas refer to Group IX. Thymolipoma 8850/0 shares its code number with liposarcoma 8850/3: the thymus tree excludes the first and refers the second.

Within Group XI: an ectopic thymoma in the lung is dealt with as a primary pulmonary tumour (ICCR, PDF p. 8), and ICD-O-3.2 prints Intrapulmonary thymoma (C34._). The thymus tree re-sites it, so the lung part (XIf4) must offer thymoma codes or a route back to this tree's thymoma options.

Within Group XI: thoracic SMARCA4-deficient undifferentiated tumour belongs to the lung chapter of the WHO thoracic volume and most often invades the mediastinum. This part's sources print no code and ICD-O-3.2 holds no term; the lung part (XIf4) and the registrar decide.

Within Group XI: thymic-type tumours of the thyroid (spindle epithelial tumour with thymus-like elements 8588/3, intrathyroid thymic carcinoma 8589/3, thymoma within the thyroid) belong to the thyroid tree. The thymus tree's 'Outside the mediastinum' option re-sites them.

Within Group XI: NUT carcinoma 8023/3 is shared with the nasopharynx, lung and NUT carcinoma parts. Whether a mediastinal NUT carcinoma records C37.9 (XIf5) or C38 (XIf10) is open (registrar question 3). The draft records the site the report gives.

data_gaps.why: Rossi 2022 settles the thymoma types A to B3 and thymoma with no type named in patients aged 0.9 to 17 years; they are now options on tm_histology. Its review excluded thymic carcinoma, thymic neuroendocrine tumours and combined thymic carcinomas (PMC section 3) and reports no metaplastic thymoma. Neither Marx 2022 nor the ICCR guide gives ages, and Pfister 2022 Table 3 lists no thymic tumour among the thoracic tumours of children, so every other thymic entity stays in tm_picker. A paediatric report would move thymic squamous cell carcinoma and the carcinoids onto tm_histology as options.

data_gaps.need: A paediatric source for the option 'Carcinoma, with no type named' (8010/3)
data_gaps.why: The option rests on the coding rule that the clerk codes what the pathologist states, not on a paediatric report, and Rossi 2022 reviews thymomas only. It stays an option; the controller decides whether a fallback option needs a paediatric report.
data_gaps.candidate_source: A paediatric thymic carcinoma series, such as Stachowicz-Stencel T, et al. Eur J Cancer 2015;51(16):2444-2452 (EXPeRT)

data_gaps.need: The order of NUT carcinoma against the thymoma options on tm_histology
data_gaps.why: Rossi 2022 gives paediatric counts for the thymoma types only. No source in this part counts thymic or mediastinal NUT carcinoma in children; its paediatric report (Pfister 2022) is in the head and neck section. The draft lists type B1 (the commonest), then types B2, AB, A and B3 by Rossi's counts, then thymoma with no type named, then NUT carcinoma.
data_gaps.candidate_source: The NUT carcinoma part's paediatric sources (Lemelle 2022)

data_gaps.need: Where the clerk records a combined thymic carcinoma and thymoma now that the two components sit on different screens
data_gaps.why: The thymoma types are options on tm_histology and the thymic carcinomas and carcinoids are tm_picker entries. The thymoma-type sentence of the Rule K hint moved to tm_histology; the two-tumour-types sentence stays on tm_picker. Rossi 2022 found no thymoma of mixed types in its paediatric cases (PMC section 5) and excluded combined thymic carcinomas (PMC section 3). Registrar question 4 decides which component is recorded, and with it which screen carries the rule.
